title: The Tortoise and the Hare
text:
The hare was proud of his speed and liked to mock the tortoise for his short legs and slow, heavy steps. One day the tortoise had heard enough. He laughed and said that, fast as the hare might be, he would beat him in a race.

The hare thought this was the funniest thing he had ever heard and agreed at once. They agreed that the fox should choose the course and set the finishing post.

When the race began, the hare shot off and was out of sight in moments. Looking back and seeing no sign of his rival, he decided there was no hurry. It was warm, the grass was soft, and he lay down by the road for a short rest. Soon he was fast asleep.

The tortoise never stopped. He did not run, because he could not, but he kept putting one foot in front of the other, mile after mile, past the sleeping hare and on toward the post.

When the hare finally woke and dashed for the finish, he was too late. The tortoise was already there, resting comfortably at the end of the course.
lesson: Talent that coasts loses to effort that keeps going. Do not judge a contest by who starts fastest, and never assume a slower rival will stop because you did.
